rationale: The analysis correctly frames the incident as a supply-side consumer-capacity failure (E1/E2), identifies the two confounded candidate causes (E3/E4), and explicitly states that the joint revert (E6) establishes causation for the change set as a whole but not for either change individually — directly matching all three required findings (non-attribution between DB wait and deserialization, joint revert, need for discriminating evidence). It never asserts either candidate as the proven primary cause, avoiding both forbidden claims. Causal structure is handled carefully: R14 explicitly marks whether both reverts were necessary as unknown, and the analysis neither invents an interaction effect nor rules one out (C11), consistent with the evidence. Claims are consistently tied to specific evidence IDs with appropriately scaled confidence (e.g., C9/C10/C12 marked medium/low as speculative extensions), and counterfactuals (X1-X6) responsibly explore how new evidence would change the conclusion. Uncertainty calibration is strong: three live alternatives (library-only, index-only, both) are preserved throughout rather than collapsed prematurely, and each uncertainty entry names a concrete discriminating observation. Action quality is excellent — A1 (single-change revert/re-application under load) is prioritized first and matches the preferred action exactly, A2/A3 add instrumentation to make that test interpretable, and A4 conservatively keeps the known-safe joint-reverted state in place rather than gambling on an unattributed re-application, which protects against harm. No unsupported outside-evidence claims, no forbidden claims, and no required findings are missed.
